questions.prompt: In this rule, which part selects the elements to style?
questions.explanation: The selector `p` matches paragraph elements; the declarations inside the braces specify their styles.

questions.prompt: What is CSS primarily used to describe?

options.text: Presentation and layout rules for documents
The server-side program that returns a page
The binary encoding of an image

questions.explanation: CSS controls presentation, including color, typography, spacing, and layout, while HTML describes document structure and meaning.

questions.prompt: Select all statements that describe a CSS rule correctly.

options.text: A selector precedes the declaration block.
A declaration pairs a property with a value.

questions.explanation: A rule has a selector and a declaration block; selectors can be types, classes, IDs, combinations, and more.

questions.prompt: Which property is being set in this declaration?
questions.explanation: In a declaration, the property name appears before the colon; `1rem` is its value.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a CSS rule to its role.
questions.explanation: A selector identifies candidate elements; each declaration names a property and its value.

questions.prompt: Which selector matches every element with class `notice`?
questions.explanation: A period begins a class selector. The class may be shared by multiple elements.

questions.prompt: Which selector matches the element whose id is `site-header`?
questions.explanation: A hash begins an ID selector; class selectors use a period.

questions.prompt: Which are CSS selectors?
questions.explanation: `padding` is a property name, not a selector.

questions.prompt: Which token pair opens a CSS comment?
questions.explanation: CSS comments begin with `/*` and end with `*/`; JavaScript-style `//` is not a CSS comment.

questions.prompt: Which at-rule condition applies styles when the viewport is at least 48rem wide?
questions.explanation: `min-width` tests whether the viewport width is at least the supplied value.

questions.prompt: Match each box-model region to its location or purpose.
questions.explanation: The content is inside the box; padding is inside the border; margin is outside.

questions.prompt: How should a page normally connect to an external stylesheet?

options.text: Put a `@link` rule in the CSS file
Use a `style` attribute on every element
Add the CSS filename as a `script` source

questions.explanation: An HTML `link` element in the document head connects an external stylesheet; it is not CSS syntax.

questions.prompt: Which declaration is discarded while the valid declaration remains applicable?

options.text: The whole rule, because one declaration is invalid
Both declarations, because CSS stops at an error

questions.explanation: CSS error recovery generally discards an invalid declaration and continues parsing later declarations in the same rule.

questions.prompt: Which properties normally inherit?
questions.explanation: Typography and text color commonly inherit; margin is box-model spacing and does not inherit by default.

questions.prompt: If two matching rules have equal cascade priority and specificity, what usually decides the winner?

options.text: The later declaration in source order
The first rule in the file

questions.explanation: When earlier cascade criteria tie, the declaration later in the relevant order wins.

questions.prompt: Match each unit to its reference.
questions.explanation: `rem` uses the root font size, `em` depends on font-size context, and `vw` uses viewport width.

questions.prompt: What is the best first response when an ordinary rule does not override another ordinary rule?

options.text: Inspect the cascade and specificity before adding `!important`
Move the rule into an inline style

questions.explanation: Debug the competing declarations, origins, layers, and specificity first; unnecessary importance makes later maintenance harder.

questions.prompt: Which property normally inherits from a parent element?
questions.explanation: Text-related properties such as `color` normally inherit; box sizing and spacing properties generally do not.

questions.prompt: Which are valid CSS length units?
questions.explanation: `rem`, `em`, and `vw` are units. `font` is a property name.

questions.prompt: Which property normally does not inherit from a parent?
questions.explanation: Margins belong to each element's box and do not inherit by default.

questions.prompt: What does `1rem` measure relative to?

options.text: The computed font size of the root element

questions.explanation: The `rem` unit is based on the root element's computed font size.

questions.prompt: Match each display value to its layout behavior.

columns.label: Flex formatting context for direct children

questions.explanation: Flexbox is primarily one-dimensional, Grid manages two dimensions, and `display: none` removes the box from layout.

questions.prompt: What does `1vw` represent?

options.text: One percent of the parent font size
One percent of the viewport width
One percent of the viewport height

questions.explanation: Viewport-width units scale with the viewport's width; `1vw` is one hundredth of that width.

questions.prompt: Which box-model region contains an element's text or other content?
questions.explanation: The content box contains the element's content; padding surrounds it inside the border.

questions.prompt: Which are parts of the CSS box model?
questions.explanation: The box consists of content, padding, border, and margin; specificity is a cascade concept.

questions.prompt: Where is padding located?

options.text: Between the content and the border

questions.explanation: Padding is the inner spacing between content and border.

questions.prompt: Match each selector to its selector category.
questions.explanation: A period selects a class, a hash selects an ID, and `:hover` is a pseudo-class.

questions.prompt: With `box-sizing: border-box`, what does a declared width include?

options.text: Content only; padding is added outside it
Content and margin, but not border

questions.explanation: Under `border-box`, the specified width includes the content, padding, and border, but not margin.

questions.prompt: What is the usual role of margin?

options.text: The width of a grid track

questions.explanation: Margins are outside the border and separate boxes from surrounding content.

questions.prompt: Which statements about flexbox are correct?

options.text: Every descendant becomes a flex item.
`display: flex` makes the element a flex container.
Its direct children become flex items.

questions.explanation: Only direct children are flex items; nested descendants participate in their own formatting contexts.

questions.prompt: What does `display: flex` establish on an element?

options.text: A two-dimensional grid for every descendant
A new document or stacking context in every case
A flex formatting context for its direct children

questions.explanation: A flex container lays out its direct children as flex items; descendants are not automatically flex items.

questions.prompt: In a flex container with the default `flex-direction`, which way does the main axis run?

options.text: Along the row, in the inline direction
Along the column, in the block direction
From the center toward each edge

questions.explanation: The initial `flex-direction` is `row`, so the main axis follows the inline direction.

questions.prompt: Match each at-rule to its common purpose.

columns.label: Defines a downloadable or local font face

questions.explanation: These at-rules respectively group conditional styles, define font faces, and define animation steps.

questions.prompt: Which CSS layout system is designed to manage rows and columns together?
questions.explanation: Grid provides two-dimensional track layout; flexbox is primarily one-dimensional.

questions.prompt: Which statements about CSS Grid are correct?

options.text: Grid can define row and column tracks.
Grid can place items into named areas.

questions.explanation: Grid is a layout system that works within the cascade; it does not replace it.

questions.prompt: What does the `gap` property set in a grid or flex container?

options.text: Spacing between its rows and columns/items
A minimum width for each item

questions.explanation: `gap` sets gutters between tracks or flex items; it does not add outer margin.

questions.prompt: Which condition is appropriate for applying a layout change only at wider viewport widths?
questions.explanation: A viewport media query can apply additional layout rules when the viewport reaches a minimum width.

questions.prompt: Which are valid media-query conditions or queries?
questions.explanation: Media features include viewport dimensions, user preferences, and input capabilities; `@query` is not a CSS at-rule.

questions.prompt: What kind of selector is `:hover`?
questions.explanation: Pseudo-classes select elements in a state or relationship; pseudo-elements address generated or specific parts.

questions.prompt: What does `::before` represent in a selector?
questions.explanation: The double-colon syntax identifies a pseudo-element such as `::before`.

questions.prompt: Which styles improve keyboard or motion accessibility?

options.text: Use more than color alone to convey state.
Remove outlines from every focused control.

questions.explanation: Visible focus, reduced-motion support, and non-color cues help users; removing all focus indication makes keyboard use harder.

questions.prompt: Which name is a valid custom property that can be read with `var()`?
questions.explanation: CSS custom property names begin with two hyphens and are consumed with `var(--brand-color)`.
